items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Sidney Catlett and Jimmy Blanton took their place in St. Louis... I had played with Jo Jones and Walter Page in St. Louis... Sidney Catlett was a great drummer.

ctx.x: Yeah, because we never got to see each other too much anyway. Of course when I joined Count Basie’s band in 1938…when I first went to New York and joined Lucky Millinder’s band and Lucky had a good band and I enjoyed playing…he had Don Byas in the band, he had Charlie Shavers, Billy Kyle who later joined Louis Armstrong and…oh he had a good band, Walter Johnson was on drums, wonderful drummer. And some reason or the other, Lucky fired me for Dizzy and that’s when I went with Basie’s band because I had played with…

Before we get too far into Count Basie, one question before we leave your early background: you said your uncle had taught you the scales, the trumpet. How did you actually learn to read music, was that from him as well, or…?

items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And then you mention that you played in the Jeter-Pillars band... Before that, they had Sid Catlett and Jimmy Blanton? ... No, after Jo Jones they had Jimmy Blanton and Sid Catlett.

ctx.x: And then you mention that you played in the Jeter-Pillars band, eventually got Jo Jones and Walter Page in it, right? Before that, they had Sid Catlett and Jimmy Blanton?
No, after Jo Jones they had Jimmy Blanton and Sid Catlett.
What was Jimmy Blanton like at that very early stage, did you hear something special in his playing even at that time?

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: Sidney Catlett and then when Sidney went back to join Fletcher Henderson in Chicago, then Jo Jones joined the band... They all used to play on the boat with Charlie Creath... And there was Sidney Catlett, he played on the boat

ctx.x: Wow, that was a good band.
